- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly above recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33), model often overcorrects downward — raise forecast modestly to avoid excessive sell-off.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) — cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods — if sentiment is neutral or mixed, forecast should be slightly above recent low to capture rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 2–3 days — adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model often fails to adjust — apply a 5–10% upward correction to avoid premature drop.
